_comment: Hand-authored. The password system: the TGL back door constant and the two credits screen scripts beside its screen text. The decode, the checksum and what is not established are in tools/password.py.

regions.name: Credits screen script
regions.description: A screen script in the format already established at bank 0 $8495 - [col][count][chars], $FF ends a row, $FE ends the script. It parses cleanly end to end as col 2 'PRODUCED BY', row, col 3 'IREM', row, col 5 'CORPORATION', with $FE at $8BA2 and the next script starting at $8BA3. That it parses at all is a free confirmation of the screen-script format on a block that was not used to derive it.

regions.name: "PASSWORD TGL" screen script
regions.description: Fifteen bytes: col 2, count 12, 'PASSWORD TGL', then $FE. THIS IS THE BACK DOOR'S OWN SCREEN. The password routine in bank 3 has a special case for the three characters T, G and L (see bank3.data_8513), and this is the text that names it, sitting immediately after the IREM credits script. WHAT THE SCREEN DOES is not established - only that the ROM contains a script that says this.

regions.name: The TGL password constant
regions.description: Three bytes, $13 $06 $0B. Those are grid indices, not ASCII: the password entry grid is A-Z then 0-9 read left to right and top to bottom, $88F2 stores a character as its grid index with LDA $16 / STA $0411,X, so A is 0 - and 19, 6, 11 is T, G, L. The on-screen grid in a password-screen savestate confirms the layout row by row. READ BY $857C: LDA $8513,Y / CMP $0411,Y for Y = 0,1,2, after which $8589 requires every character from index 3 to $1F to be zero. On a match $8592 sets $2F = 0 and $30 = 2 and returns with carry clear, SKIPPING THE CHECKSUM at $859B entirely. $30 is the game-mode byte. Bounded by its reader's operand and by the code either side: $8512 is an RTS and $8516 is a traced instruction start, so these three bytes are exactly the gap between. A CONSEQUENCE OF THE ENCODING, stated because the code says so and not because it was tried: a blank and the letter A are both the byte 0 - the savestate shows an untouched field is all $00 - so 'TGL' followed by any number of A's is the same 32 bytes as 'TGL' followed by blanks, and this check cannot tell them apart.
